description:
Implement the agreed Channel-node file delivery architecture from https://chatgpt.com/space/page_1e1079bf6234819185ccfa7aecefadc8 after the Mattermost prerequisite fixes. This is the durable execution plan; the Page supplies the reviewed design/diagrams. Planning only now, no implementation or application Git publication.
Target: /Users/jad/Desktop/Jad/workspace/zaq/forks/jat10/zaq-feat-channel-files.
External predecessor: ../workspace-planning work-pim. Reuse its adapter fixes and work-pim.6 pin/lock task; do not duplicate provider implementation.
Supersedes obsolete delivery architecture in zaq-juu and zaq-ucc and historical dependency test issue zaq-7kl. Closing superseded tasks is administrative replacement, not a claim that their work passed. Retain completed historical evidence and carry forward relevant correctness obligations. Keep unrelated Agent trusted-context task zaq-ucc.20 and deferred backend persistence-contract task zaq-ucc.11 open. Keep broader feature zaq-ic9, Agent/access tasks and existing PR-distribution epic zaq-rn4.
Preserved legacy checks: content-free Records plus private-plan removal; permissive Outgoing builder; shared posting/option construction; real provider post IDs; default HTTP edit behavior; frozen selected SMTP connector and policy; prepared SMTP display metadata with no source IDs; existing Engine form snapshot; canonical fallback confirmation. Verify these in contracts/Jido/email/history/journey issues, without reinstating obsolete adapter-owned orchestration.
Policy owners: AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/documentation.md and affected service guides. New SMTP UI requires DESIGN.md and BO rules.
Dependency DAG intentionally converges: SMTP settings and shared executor are both required for email; Jido and email both required for unified confirmation. No other diamond is needed. Only the external verification gate is initially ready; implementation waits for it. Separate UX, consolidated E2E, review and post-review coverage gates remain explicit.

# Scope and agreed decisions

- Preserve AttachDocuments, its validation and destination preflight, StreamEvents selection, and attachment_error. No Agent behavior changes.

- Preserve incoming files, signed materialization handles, trusted actor authorization, notification/workflow producers, and existing Engine history ownership.

- Every communication Outgoing enters DeliveryFiles, including an outgoing carrying attachment_error. DeliveryFiles normalizes Agent selection failures and preparation failures into the same policy flow. Ordinary text-only messages with no attachment failure pass through unchanged; Channels API has no separate attachment-error branch.

- Resolve FileRequirements through the selected bridge and actual connection configuration. No guessed provider limits. Configuration can tighten a known provider limit, never raise it.

- Materialize files before execution starts. Keep bytes in memory and do not delete source files or introduce temporary-file storage.

- Start with ordered grouping, filling each message until count or size limits are reached. Fifteen files with a ten-file limit become ten plus five. Keep the grouping function replaceable for later size-aware packing; do not reorder files now.

- Failure policy comes from existing send_on_file_failure settings: continue or stop. Keep the existing internal :abort value for stop to avoid an unnecessary configuration migration.

- Stop materialization/configuration failures before delivery. Continue omits failed attachments, sends usable ones, and reports failures. If none remain, send the original text.

- For separately uploadable files, stop policy uploads all groups before any new publication. An upload failure prevents publication. Already streamed text and completed uploads may remain.

- Publication is sequential under stop policy. Under continue policy, independent ready operations may run with bounded concurrency.

- Continue reports failed or unconfirmed sends and proceeds to other groups. With no confirmed root ID, try the next group as root. Never retry the failed group or redistribute its files.

- Thread remaining groups under an existing thread root, or under the first successful newly created root. If threading is unsupported, send independent messages. Initial placement strategy is hardcoded and capability-driven; a configurable strategy can follow.

- Reuse an existing message when attachment edits are supported. Plans may also send a message first and attach files through a later edit. Stop policy still places uploads before new publication.

- Reuse DeliveryConfirmation and Engine recording. Confirm only actual successful sends/edits and their delivered attachments.

- Add two SMTP inputs: maximum encoded message size in MB, and maximum attachments per message. No provider-specific default values.

- No automatic delivery retries, rollback, orphan-upload cleanup, automatic SMTP discovery, or new agent tools in this iteration.

# Route through the Channel node

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P["Agent or notification producer"] --> E["Outgoing in Event"]
  E --> N["NodeRouter dispatch to Channels Api"]
  subgraph C["Channel node"]
    N --> R["Resolve communication bridge and exact connection"]
    R --> D["DeliveryFiles entry for every communication Outgoing"]
    D --> A{"Attachments to prepare"}
    A -- No --> ERR{"attachment_error present"}
    ERR -- No --> PASS["Return Outgoing unchanged"]
    PASS --> OLD["Existing bridge delivery path"]
    ERR -- Yes --> F["Normalize Agent selection failure"]
    A -- Yes --> Q["Normalize any selection failure and resolve bridge file_requirements"]
    Q -- Resolved --> M["Materialize and validate actual files"]
    Q -- Configuration failure --> V["Apply shared preparation policy"]
    M --> G["Plan message groups and upload batches using exact sizing"]
    G -- Prepared groups and any planning failures --> V
    F --> V
    V -- Stop with failures --> STOP["Report failure without execution"]
    V -- Continue or no failures --> B["Set delivery_plan with usable groups or text-only failure outcome"]
    B --> X["Shared DeliveryExecutor"]
    X --> J["JidoChatBridge operations"]
    X --> I["EmailBridge operations"]
    J --> JA["One planned upload request or one post send or edit"]
    I --> SM["Existing SMTP sender and MIME preparation"]
    JA --> O["Normalized operation outcomes"]
    SM --> O
    O --> X
    X --> DR["Shared delivery report including preparation failures"]
    STOP --> DR
    DR --> DC["DeliveryConfirmation for confirmed outcomes only"]
    OLD --> DC
  end
  DC --> H["Existing Engine record_delivery_confirmation event"]
```

Connection resolution remains authoritative and happens once per attempt. In particular, an IMAP route retains its conversation identity while binding the selected SMTP sender and that sender’s settings. The executor must not switch connectors halfway through a plan.

DeliveryFiles owns preparation, message grouping, upload-request batch planning, and applying resolved failure policy to selection/preparation outcomes. DeliveryExecutor applies that policy during transport execution. Channels API resolves the bridge and connection without an attachment-error bypass. Bridges translate operations and outcomes. Mattermost validates provider constraints, confirms identities, normalizes metadata, and supplies exact multipart sizing/encoding. Its upload primitive submits one explicitly planned request; it does not choose batches, create extra posts, route continuations, or apply publication policy.

The existing :validate_files route used by AttachDocuments remains separate and compatible. Introducing file_requirements must not change the Agent action’s validation contract.

# Requirements and preparation contracts

The bridge returns FileRequirements, combining provider constraints and channel configuration. Keep limits separate from strategies: requirements say what is possible; the plan says what to do.

```elixir
# Proposed ZAQ contract
defmodule Zaq.Channels.FileRequirements do
  @enforce_keys [:max_files_per_message, :transfer_mode]
  defstruct [
    :max_files_per_message,
    :max_file_bytes,
    :max_attachment_bytes_per_message,
    :max_encoded_message_bytes,
    :max_upload_request_bytes,
    :transfer_mode,
    supports_threads: false,
    supports_attachment_edits: false
  ]
end

# Proposed bridge callback
@callback file_requirements(Outgoing.t(), map()) ::
  {:ok, FileRequirements.t()} | {:error, DeliveryError.t()}
```

transfer_mode is :upload_then_publish or :send_with_files. A field is a positive resolved limit, explicitly :not_applicable where the protocol has no separate constraint, or unresolved and rejected when needed. Missing must not silently mean unlimited. The contract task must define those representations precisely and validate them.

JidoChatBridge obtains provider requirements from an optional shared adapter callback. Do not put numeric limits into Jido’s capability matrix: its current values are :native, :fallback, and :unsupported. The adapter callback returns SDK-owned data; the bridge maps it into ZAQ’s struct. Jido must not depend on ZAQ modules.

EmailBridge resolves the two SMTP settings. File-count settings can be deliberate deployment limits even when the provider publishes no count ceiling. Do not label a locally chosen value as a Gmail limit.

```elixir
# Illustrative API flow, not executable code.
# The existing confirmation boundary consumes the returned outcome.
with {:ok, connection} <- resolve_delivery_connection(outgoing),
     {:ok, prepared_outgoing} <-
       DeliveryFiles.build_plan(outgoing, bridge, connection) do
  case prepared_outgoing.delivery_plan do
    nil ->
      # Ordinary text only: preserve the existing bridge delivery path.
      bridge.send_reply(prepared_outgoing, connection)

    %DeliveryPlan{} ->
      DeliveryExecutor.execute(prepared_outgoing, bridge, connection)
  end
end
# Stop-policy preparation failures return an error/report from build_plan;
# neither delivery branch runs.
```

build_plan immediately returns {:ok, outgoing} unchanged when attachments is empty and attachment_error is nil. This fast path does not look up file requirements, normalize failure evidence, materialize, group, create a plan, or invoke DeliveryExecutor. Otherwise it normalizes existing Agent attachment_error into failure evidence and processes eligible attachments through shared preparation policy. It reuses Record validation, trusted context, Materialization.materialize/3, and validated DecodeBase64 Action execution. Resolve file requirements only when there are files to prepare; validate actual acquired metadata and sizes before grouping. A rejected Agent selection remains a selection failure, not a per-file materialization failure. Preparation performs no upload or send.

Unknown file requirements produce structured configuration failures inside DeliveryFiles. Stop blocks the attachment-bearing outgoing. Continue skips all attachments and may plan text delivery if connection and text requirements are valid. A missing connection blocks both policies. A planned text-only fallback must respect any applicable resolved encoded-message ceiling; continue does not authorize an oversized body. Ordinary text-only messages without attachment_error bypass file planning entirely and retain existing bridge behavior; this work must not add a file-requirements lookup or new mandatory attachment settings to that path.

## Upload request sizing and batch planning

Message groups and upload batches are different. Ten files assigned to one message might require two upload requests. Both batches remain assigned to that same message group. DeliveryFiles chooses those batches; the executor invokes the upload primitive once for each planned batch. No adapter or transport loop invents extra upload requests.

Extend FileRequirements with an explicit upload-request byte ceiling when separate upload is supported. Do not derive that ceiling from a per-file limit without a documented provider rule. Multipart overhead depends on the actual encoded representation, so raw file sizes cannot prove a batch fits.

Expose a side-effect-free provider sizing/preparation operation through the bridge. It encodes or measures exactly the proposed candidate batch; it does not split candidates or perform network I/O. DeliveryFiles uses that result to fill batches. Reuse the existing ReqClient multipart implementation; do not duplicate MIME boundaries, headers, or allowance constants in ZAQ.

```elixir
# Proposed boundary; finalize names in prerequisite Task 0A.
bridge.prepare_upload_request(candidate_files, connection)
# => {:ok, %{encoded_bytes: count, request: opaque_prepared_request}}
# => {:error, provider_validation_error}

bridge.upload_prepared_request(opaque_prepared_request, connection)
# => one HTTP upload attempt with stable per-input outcomes
```

Prepared requests are private transient values and must use the same encoded representation when submitted. If a candidate exceeds the request ceiling, the planner tries a smaller candidate before execution; an individual file that cannot fit becomes a preparation failure. Exact-limit, one-byte-over, and multipart-header-heavy cases must be covered. Request preparation, sizing, and grouping failures enter the same preparation-policy gate as materialization failures: stop executes nothing; continue excludes affected files and retains their original indices in the report.

A send/edit depends on every planned upload batch for its group. Stop additionally waits for all groups’ uploads to succeed before any publication. Continue can omit failed files using normalized outcomes; the adapter never decides to publish a partial message. Partial request outcomes retain only provider-confirmed facts, not inferred success or automatic retries.

# Delivery plan and runtime state

Add a nullable delivery_plan field to Outgoing, populated only on the Channel node. It is transient execution data, never model input, public metadata, checkpoint content, or persisted history. Ordinary text-only outgoing messages with no attachment_error retain delivery_plan: nil and take the existing bridge path. A text-only outcome caused by an attachment failure under continue carries a plan and failure evidence; it is not ordinary text passthrough. Stop-policy preparation failures return without executing a plan.

Keep the plan descriptive and runtime results separate. Steps reference prior outputs rather than mutating identifiers into unrelated metadata.

```elixir
# Proposed module layout and schematic fields
defmodule Zaq.Channels.DeliveryPlan do
  defstruct [
    :failure_policy,
    :placement,
    :root_message_id,
    files: %{},
    groups: [],
    steps: [],
    preparation_failures: []
  ]

  defmodule Step do
    defstruct [
      :id, :operation, :group_id,
      :message_ref, :file_refs,
      depends_on: []
    ]
  end
end

# A group uploaded then attached to an existing message
[
  %DeliveryPlan.Step{
    id: :upload_1, operation: :upload, group_id: 1,
    file_refs: [0, 1, 2]
  },
  %DeliveryPlan.Step{
    id: :edit_1, operation: :edit, group_id: 1,
    message_ref: {:existing, "provider-message-id"},
    file_refs: {:result, :upload_1, :uploaded_files},
    depends_on: [:upload_1]
  }
]
```

Original attachment indices remain stable through preparation, grouping, partial uploads, and reporting. Keep one authoritative prepared file collection; steps reference it. Exact encoding may allocate additional transient request/MIME buffers, so this design does not promise one physical copy of each byte. Opaque prepared requests stay private to the attempt and must not serialize credentials or trusted context into plan descriptions.

Thread root election is an executor rule over ordered root candidates. It cannot be represented solely by a static “depend on first send” edge: if the first candidate fails, the next must become eligible. A successful root unlocks remaining replies.

Proposed bridge surface:

```elixir
@callback execute_delivery_step(Step.t(), map(), map()) ::
  {:ok, map()} | {:error, DeliveryError.t(), map()}
```

The middle argument contains resolved step inputs; the last is the frozen connection. Normalize outputs as uploaded file references, confirmed message receipts, and failures with original indices, stage, safe reason, and certainty. Upload success is not message delivery. Confirmed root IDs must come from valid provider evidence; a generated fallback or correlation ID is not confirmation of a remotely created message. The step callback dispatches each :upload step to the one-request upload primitive; these are layers of the same operation, not two network calls.

Reuse existing DeliveryError and receipt/report fields rather than inventing a competing error model. Add only fields needed for configuration failures, step identity, uploaded-only evidence, and unattempted outcomes. Bridges must not invoke the whole delivery path recursively or apply their own continue/stop policy.

# Execution and dependencies

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  PREP["All materialization completed"] --> POLICY{"Failure policy"}
  POLICY -- Stop --> UP["Execute every planned upload batch where supported"]
  UP --> UOK{"Every upload successful"}
  UOK -- No --> STOP["Stop and report uploads and failures"]
  UOK -- Yes --> S1["Publish group 1"]
  S1 --> OK1{"Confirmed"}
  OK1 -- No --> END["Stop and mark later groups not attempted"]
  OK1 -- Yes --> S2["Publish later groups sequentially; stop on first failure"]
  POLICY -- Continue --> READY["Run independent ready operations with bounded concurrency"]
  READY --> ROOT{"Thread root needed"}
  ROOT -- No --> PAR["Publish independent messages"]
  ROOT -- Yes --> CAND["Try next ordered root candidate"]
  CAND -- Failed or unconfirmed --> NEXT["Report candidate outcome"]
  NEXT --> LEFT{"Another candidate remains"}
  LEFT -- Yes --> CAND
  LEFT -- No --> DONE["Finish report with no confirmed root"]
  CAND -- Confirmed ID --> REPLIES["Unlock remaining thread replies"]
```

The root-candidate loop ends when one candidate succeeds or none remain. For continue, a timeout remains unconfirmed; it is not reclassified as definitely unsent. Promotion is still allowed by the agreed policy. The uncertain earlier message may exist remotely and is not retried.

Keep publication sequential for stop, including dependent send/edit steps. An existing streamed message is not rolled back. If text creation succeeds but attachment editing fails, report confirmed text and failed or unconfirmed file attachment separately.

For stop uploads, initially prefer sequential planned upload batches across groups for simple “stop starting work” behavior. This is an implementation proposal; the agreed invariant is that every upload completes successfully before publication. Email and other :send_with_files transports cannot pre-upload: all preparation completes first, then each combined send runs sequentially under stop.

For continue, concurrency is bounded by runtime configuration, not an unbounded Task.async_stream. Use an existing appropriate task supervisor after discovery, preserve per-attempt isolation, and collect results in stable plan order. Transport retries must be disabled where configurable; a task timeout after a request started produces unconfirmed delivery.

After a root exists, continue-mode replies may run in parallel. Their visible arrival order is not guaranteed. No operation is submitted twice within an execution attempt.

# Mattermost examples

## Fifteen attachments and a five file limit

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant X as ZAQ executor
  participant B as JidoChatBridge
  participant M as Mattermost adapter
  loop Each upload batch planned by ZAQ
    X->>B: Execute prepared upload batch
    B->>M: Submit one upload request
    M-->>B: Confirmed file IDs or operation failure
    B-->>X: Normalized batch outcome
  end
  X->>B: Publish files 1 to 5 as root
  B->>M: Create post with file IDs
  M-->>X: Failure or unconfirmed result
  Note over X: Continue policy reports first group and promotes second
  X->>B: Publish files 6 to 10 as root
  B->>M: Create post with file IDs
  M-->>X: Confirmed message ID R
  X->>B: Publish files 11 to 15 under R
  B->>M: Create reply with root ID R
  M-->>X: Confirmed reply
```

Files 1–5 are not redistributed or retried. Files 6–10 form the successful root; files 11–15 form its reply. If an existing root was already supplied, root promotion is unnecessary and all groups target that root.

## Existing message and attachment edits

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EXIST["Existing streamed message ID"] --> EDIT["Edit message with final text and confirmed file IDs"]
  UP["Execute planned upload batches for first group"] --> EDIT
  EDIT --> RESULT{"Edit outcome and policy"}
  RESULT -- Confirmed --> MORE["Execute remaining groups with known root ID"]
  RESULT -- Failure or unconfirmed under continue --> REPORT["Report edit outcome and continue remaining groups"]
  REPORT --> MORE
  RESULT -- Failure or unconfirmed under stop --> STOP["Stop and report; preserve existing message"]
```

When a plan creates text first, it contains Send → Edit and Upload → Edit dependencies. Under continue, upload and text creation may be independently ready; under stop, uploads precede creation. When supported, creating a new message with already uploaded IDs is also valid and avoids an unnecessary edit.

The capability for attachment editing means “attach to an existing message,” not “send a file.” Telegram and Discord’s inspected send_file paths create messages; they do not automatically supply the separate-upload protocol. Those adapters use the combined-send mode unless their actual contracts are extended.

Mattermost changes are a prerequisite: remove automatic message splitting, generated continuation text, continuation routing, orchestration reports, publication-policy options/capabilities, and automatic HTTP upload-batch selection. Preserve provider checks and exact multipart encoding/measurement. Expose one-request upload and single-post create/edit-with-uploaded-references primitives. ZAQ explicitly plans multiple upload requests when necessary and combines their confirmed IDs into the intended message.

# Email requirements and MIME sizing

Add these inputs to the selected SMTP connector:

| Input | Meaning | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum message size in MB | Complete encoded message including body, MIME headers, boundaries, and attachments | Positive explicit value, converted to bytes using a documented unit |
| Maximum attachments per message | Maximum files in one email | Positive integer |

Use MB as 1,000,000 bytes in UI conversion and store an unambiguous byte value. Preserve missing values as missing for existing connectors; do not backfill a guessed Gmail limit. File requirements errors follow the agreed policy. Ordinary text-only delivery with no attachment_error bypasses file_requirements and retains existing behavior even on legacy connectors with missing attachment settings. Planned fallback text remains distinct and follows applicable resolved limits.

EmailBridge uses :send_with_files: each group becomes one SMTP submission with its own attachment set. The shared executor owns grouping, sequencing, continue/stop, and results. EmailBridge owns envelope recipients, subject, MIME representation, and email-specific thread headers.

Swoosh currently renders the MIME body inside its SMTP adapter before calling gen_smtp_client.send_blocking. Its Helpers module is marked internal. The implementation must establish a narrow supported or version-pinned preparation/submission seam; it must not copy Swoosh’s MIME encoder or build a second mail-composition path.

Prefer preparing and measuring the same MIME bytes that will be submitted. A simple raw-byte sum or fixed “plus 33 percent” cannot prove the complete message fits. The bridge should provide candidate-message preparation/sizing to the shared grouping logic. Preserve text/HTML bodies, selected SMTP identity, recipients, MIME types, and filenames.

Thread references may change when another group becomes the root. Freeze generated message IDs and deterministic headers where possible, then revalidate the final encoded payload after dependency resolution and before SMTP submission. If it no longer fits, return a size failure handled by policy; never send an oversized payload. The exact reusable MIME seam is a contract checkpoint before email implementation, not permission to estimate silently.

Disable gen_smtp automatic retries for these attempts. The inspected dependency defaults to one retry; current sender options do not override it. SMTP acceptance confirms submission to the relay, not arrival in the recipient’s inbox.

SMTP SIZE can advertise a whole-message limit, but discovery is deferred. The recipient’s server may impose a lower limit even after the sender relay accepts a message. These do not justify hardcoded provider limits.

Sources: [SMTP SIZE standard](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1870.html), [MIME encoding standard](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2045), [Gmail attachment guidance](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/6584?hl=en), [Exchange message and attachment limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/exchange-online-service-description/exchange-online-limits). Advertised raw attachment limits and encoded-message limits are different configuration concepts.

# Reporting and existing history integration

The executor produces one normalized report. Preserve the existing messages, confirmation, and failed_files conventions where compatible. Add separate uploaded-only evidence and unattempted step/group outcomes; retain raw internal reasons privately and expose only safe reasons.

```elixir
# Schematic report for partial success
%{
  confirmation: :partial,
  messages: [
    %{message_id: "root", confirmation: :confirmed,
      thread_id: nil, delivered_attachment_indices: [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]},
    %{message_id: "reply", confirmation: :confirmed,
      thread_id: "root", delivered_attachment_indices: [10, 11, 12, 13, 14]}
  ],
  failed_files: [
    %{attachment_index: 0, stage: :transport,
      delivery: :unconfirmed, reason: :timeout}
    # Include each affected original index, not just the first.
  ],
  unattempted_steps: []
}
```

DeliveryConfirmation.record/3 already accepts a messages list and dispatches individual :record_delivery_confirmation events. Its tests already cover partial reports, original-index filtering, provider evidence precedence, and bookkeeping failures. Reuse this path.

Each confirmed receipt carries its actual body, thread identity, action, and delivered attachment metadata. A successful edit updates the existing canonical message rather than inserting a duplicate. A text send followed by a failed edit must not claim attachment delivery. Multiple outcomes for the same provider message must compose in operation order.

Provider media descriptors remain authoritative for chat. SMTP uses display metadata and selected original indices without inventing remote download references. Never persist source handles as delivered provider references.

Explicitly clear delivery_plan before the confirmation copy crosses to Engine. Clearing Record.content alone is insufficient because the new plan can hold prepared bytes. Also exclude it from inspection, telemetry, public projections, and failure logging.

History recording failure remains a bookkeeping failure after transport success. It never resends a message. Notification reply callbacks and status updates must retain their existing cardinality and final-ID semantics; per-step execution must not accidentally multiply callbacks.

# Existing tests to preserve and behavior changes to approve

Reuse existing files, fixture builders, real materialization, transport stubs, and assertion helpers. Add a new suite only when it owns a distinct new contract, such as scheduler properties, that is awkward to validate in an existing suite.

| Existing coverage | Keep or extend |
| --- | --- |
| DeliveryFiles authorization and byte properties | Keep all access, provenance, encoding, order, and source-preservation assertions |
| attachment_policy_test.exs | Extend preparation policy scenarios to grouping and shared execution |
| jido_chat_delivery_test.exs | Move orchestration expectations to ZAQ; keep actual provider request assertions |
| SMTP outgoing and sender suites | Extend current byte, MIME, recipients, sender, and threading checks to multiple groups |
| delivery_confirmation_test.exs | Reuse multi-message partial reporting and original-index tests; add plan stripping |
| Existing history and Agent journeys | Prove recorded results and later access without changing Agent selection behavior |

Specific existing expectations that will change must be disclosed and approved before editing tests, per `docs/testing-approach.md`:

1. “adapter-owned splitting returns separate receipts for all fifteen files” becomes ZAQ-owned splitting with single-message adapter operations.

2. “configured limit reaches the adapter … without bridge file planning” becomes bridge-supplied constraints consumed by DeliveryFiles.

3. “strict policy rejects an adapter … no policy support” becomes rejection only when required transport operations/requirements are missing; the adapter no longer needs to own policy.

4. “explicit policy reaches attachment create and edit” becomes policy retained and enforced in ZAQ, not forwarded upstream.

5. “final create and edit failures … without replacement delivery” keeps no retry of that failed group, but permits later groups and root promotion under continue, including unconfirmed results.

6. Adapter policy/splitting and transport automatic-batching suites change during prerequisite Task 0B. Preserve provider regressions, replace host-orchestration expectations with single-operation boundary checks, and catalogue the moved scenarios for ZAQ policy/delivery suites. This includes the newly agreed single-request upload boundary, which is stricter than the reviewer’s allowance. Obtain explicit approval for these test behavior changes; never simply delete their coverage.

7. SMTP fixtures that previously omitted limits need explicit values when attachment delivery requires them; disclose fixture changes that alter behavior rather than treating them as mechanical setup.

The discussion approves the intended architectural direction. It does not automatically satisfy the repository’s explicit existing-test-behavior approval gate for every undisclosed assertion change.

Property tests should target invariants, not mirror the implementation: count/byte bounds, complete original-index accounting, once-only execution, resolved dependencies, no forbidden publication, and absence of private prepared data in confirmations.

# Implementation checkpoints and acceptance

Before execution, resolve dependency callback names in Task 0A, adopt verified revisions in Task 1, and finalize ZAQ contracts and the MIME preparation seam in Task 2. Confirm how continuation bodies, subjects, and reply callbacks preserve current semantics, particularly when the original first group fails. A proposed default is to carry the original answer on the promoted root when it has not already been confirmed, and use existing continuation wording for later groups. Do not silently duplicate a previously streamed answer or omit it after promotion.

For email, a globally configured message ceiling does not prove the recipient will accept it, and two SMTP inputs do not describe every provider-specific content restriction. Known additional provider constraints can be surfaced by requirements or provider failures; no invented Gmail count/size values belong in the defaults.

Acceptance requires:

- One planner and one executor used by both bridges. ZAQ also selects upload-request batches; Mattermost measures/encodes and executes each planned upload request without hidden splitting.

- No attachment upload before materialization finishes.

- No publication after any failed upload under stop when separate uploads exist.

- Sequential stop publication; bounded independent continue execution.

- Root promotion and original-index failure reporting as agreed, with unknown outcomes retained as unknown.

- No automatic retry, source deletion, cross-connector switching, or leaked prepared bytes.

- Accurate existing Engine confirmation behavior for every actual delivered message.

- Explicit SMTP limits and exact encoded-payload size validation.

- Preservation of Agent validation, authorization, adapter metadata preflight, and ordinary text-only routing: return unchanged with no plan and no requirements, materialization, grouping, or executor invocation.

- Focused existing test extensions, disclosed expectation changes, and validated independent PRs.

Future work remains separate: retries and reconciliation of unconfirmed sends, smarter packing/reordering, configurable placement strategies, automatic SMTP limit discovery, streaming materialization/memory budgets, and cleanup of orphaned provider uploads.
title: [zaq-1lw] Implement shared Channel file delivery plans
